decision.explanation: The supplied evidence (pmid-25295501) describes a single case of anaplastic thyroid cancer, a subtype of thyroid gland adenocarcinoma, where acquired resistance to everolimus (a Serine/Threonine Kinase Inhibitor) was associated with the emergence of the MTOR F2108L mutation. The mutation was detected in the resistant tumor tissue but was undetectable in the pretreatment tumor, confirming its role as a mechanism of resistance. The claim accurately reflects the disease, molecular profile, variant origin, drug class, and significance as reported in the source.

citations.quote:
After 18 months of a sustained response to everolimus, scans revealed progressive disease (Fig. 1E). The patient underwent a mediastinoscopy with removal of an enlarged lymph node, which contained metastatic anaplastic thyroid cancer (Fig. 1B, and Fig. S1 in Supplementary Appendix 1). Whole-exome sequencing was performed on biopsy samples of the pretreatment and resistant tumors as well as on a blood sample. . . . Figure 2
Mutations in TSC2 and MTOR in Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma Revealed by Whole-Exome Sequencing

Whole-exome sequencing of the tumor tissue before treatment and after the development of resistance to everolimus revealed a TSC2 nonsense mutation in both tumors (Panel A) and an F2108L mutation in MTOR in the resistant tumor that was undetectable in the pretreatment tumor (Panel B).
